quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should turn their heads to look over their shoulders. Why?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can get the attention of other drivers by turning their heads.
Mirrors are not helpful.
They should try to make eye contact with nearby drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that you cannot see in your mirrors. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is true about making eye contact with other drivers?

options.text: It is the best way to know that they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not mean they will give you the right of way when they should.
It guarantees they will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will give you the right of way when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will give you the right of way. Drivers often look at a motorcycle but do not notice it is there.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other traffic. Be extra alert where another vehicle may cross in front of you.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:

options.text: Have scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely.

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, allow clear views to both sides, and fasten securely. It should allow air to pass through. An airtight face shield can fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders must wear a helmet.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Helmets greatly reduce the risk of serious head injury, but they are not legally required in Illinois. However, wearing a helmet is highly recommended.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean as the operator leans. They should sit as close to the operator as possible without crowding them, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after you have started the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you have started the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before you ride. Have them get on only after the engine has started. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you usually do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, avoid riding in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this can depend on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, often in the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT lower your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be visible.
Signal your intentions.
Be ready to react to hazards.
Hope another driver sees you.

questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, you must be visible and signal your intentions. You must also watch for hazards and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you—take action to make yourself visible.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always avoid the left side of the lane.
Always avoid the right side of the lane.
Always avoid the center of the lane.
Use whichever position is safest for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever position is safest for current conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you should always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
Move back and forth across the lane as they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back too soon.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by vehicles ahead of you. The left tire track is usually best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.
